transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
Hello, doctor. I’m exhausted all the time, like I’m running on empty no matter how much I rest, and I just don’t have the energy to keep up with anything anymore.
Do you find it difficult to fall asleep or stay asleep at night, or do you sleep for a normal amount of time and still feel exhausted?

I actually try to rest plenty and go to bed early, but it doesn't seem to make a difference. I wake up feeling completely wiped out, almost like I've already worked a double shift before the day even starts. Even doing simple things around the house leaves me totally exhausted and needing to sit down.
Along with this extreme exhaustion, have you also been feeling persistently down, or have you lost interest in the activities you usually enjoy?

Yes, I've been feeling really down, and I've completely lost interest in the things I used to love doing. I've stopped going to my woodworking class and the anglers club, and I don't even touch my fishing rods anymore. Most days I just sit in my recliner feeling completely empty and disconnected from everything.
How long have you been experiencing this constant exhaustion and feeling of being down?
It's been going on for well over a year now, ever since they announced the restructuring at my work. It's just been this continuous, heavy weight that hasn't let up for a single day.
You mentioned this has been going on for well over a year. Has it been two years or longer, or has it not quite reached that point yet?
No, it hasn't quite been two full years yet, but it's been about a year and a half. Ever since they announced the changes at my job, it's just been a slow, heavy slide down to where I am now.
During this difficult time, have you also been struggling with feelings of worthlessness, or finding yourself blaming yourself and feeling excessively guilty?

Yes, I feel like my whole life has been a waste and that I failed my family by never doing anything bigger than cleaning buildings. I keep replaying every little mistake I've ever made in my head, and I even blame myself for the upcoming layoffs at work. I can't help but feel like they are happening because I just wasn't good enough at my job.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of feeling very down, exhausted, and losing interest in things at any other point in your life before this started a year and a half ago?

No, I've never felt anything like this before in my entire life. It all only started about a year and a half ago when I began planning for retirement and heard about the restructuring at my job. Before that, I was always able to keep up with my work and enjoy my hobbies just fine.
During this difficult time, have you had any thoughts of death, felt like you would be better off dead, or had any thoughts of hurting yourself?

To be honest, I've had those thoughts quite a bit lately, and some nights I lie in bed just wishing I wouldn't wake up. I've even pictured driving my car off the highway or taking too many of my blood pressure pills. But I haven't actually made a plan or tried to do anything like that.
Are you still able to manage your daily responsibilities and take care of yourself, even if it is very difficult? Or have you found yourself completely unable to do these things?

It's gotten incredibly hard to keep up, and I've started missing shifts and leaving my cleaning tasks half-finished, which actually led to a warning from my supervisor. I've also completely let my house go and have been neglecting my own grooming because I just feel too frozen and drained to do anything.
Have you noticed that your physical movements, speech, or thinking have slowed down significantly, perhaps to the point where others have commented on it?

Yes, I've noticed that quite a bit. Sometimes I find myself completely frozen in one spot, like in the hallway at work or in my kitchen, just staring at the floor for ten or fifteen minutes. If someone tries to talk to me, it takes me a long time to move or answer because my whole body feels like it's stuck in molasses.
Have you recently heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see, or held strong beliefs that others told you were not true?

Yes, actually... it's hard to admit, but at night when I'm alone, I often hear a low male voice whispering my name and calling me a failure. I've also become convinced that management at my work is quietly tracking everything I do and say, even when I'm at home, to make sure I'm pushed out of my job.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the criteria for a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms (F32.3). He presents with a 1.5-year history of persistent depressed mood, profound anhedonia, and severe fatigue. This is accompanied by cognitive and physical symptoms of depression, including severe feelings of worthlessness/guilt, psychomotor retardation (freezing and feeling 'stuck in molasses'), and suicidal ideation. Crucially, he also experiences mood-congruent psychotic symptoms, including auditory hallucinations (a voice calling him a failure) and persecutory delusions (believing his employer is tracking him at home). Since this is his first episode, a single episode code is appropriate.
